text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Kabariti, visiting Central Bank, says economic liberalisation must continue. Bank governor Fariz says bank plans to activate money markets and increase transparency.
- King Hussein to visit Egyptian President Mubarak in first direct Arab reaction to stalled Hebron talks since departure of U.S. envoy Ross.
- Cabinet accepts gift from West Bank of olive oil to help cover local requirements.
- Korean car company to assemble cars in Jordan.
- Kidnapped baby returned to her parents a month after she was taken from her mother in hospital.
- Sources say Israeli President Weizman will visit Jordan within a week to discuss tensions caused by lack of implementation of Palestinian-Israeli agreements.
- Elections next February will cover 21 municipalities
- Corruption prevention body registers fewer cases of financial corruption and violations in September.
- Trade Minister Abu al-Ragheb says in Geneva he hopes Jordanian membership of World Trade Organisation will boost exports. Jordan began negotiations to join the WTO on Monday.
- Government rejects human rights report as a political statement. Says there have been "some violations" but Jordan's human rights records comparable with Europe.
